reason: E3 confirms the baseline SFE and the general principle that SFE governs deformation mechanisms, but none of the cited evidence directly supports the key premise that removing Ni reduces SFE in this specific alloy system. E1 and E2 discuss different alloy compositions and do not address the Ni-removal effect.
premises: Removing Ni from Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni reduces stacking fault energy (SFE)
SFE changes alter dislocation nucleation, cross-slip, and twinning activity
These dislocation changes modulate strength-ductility balance
Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni has intermediate SFE (~25-30 mJ/m²) promoting twinning
Nanoindentation and in situ TEM can quantify SFE and dislocation behavior differences
